summary: We reviewed local reports and organizational information to understand the gap.

open_questions: What new local evidence changes the starting picture?

title: Investigating why dogs get stuck
summary: We're examining what prevents dogs in Stockton from reaching safe care—from street response and shelter intake to veterinary treatment, fostering, rescue, and adoption.

next_step.title: Investigate immediate suffering among street dogs
next_step.summary: Review reported locations and existing feeding efforts, then safely observe conditions firsthand. Determine whether dogs face urgent unmet needs and whether additional help is needed.

open_questions: Where do dogs get stuck between a street report and safe placement, and why?
How do street response, shelter capacity, veterinary care, rescue, and pet-inclusive housing fit together?
Where could technology, intelligence, or better coordination remove a practical constraint so more dogs receive care?
What new capacity is actually becoming available, and when will it become operational?
Which barriers will each project relieve, and which will remain?
What practical help is needed to accelerate or operate each project?

initial_map.summary: What we're investigating now: whether residents can reach the right people and obtain help; which shelter, foster, and veterinary constraints limit safe care; and whether communication, scheduling, volunteer onboarding, or placement coordination can improve. These are preliminary questions. Fieldwork and verified data will test them.

threads.title: Street response and intake
threads.summary: Follow what happens when someone reports or finds a stray dog, from the first request for help to a safe intake or other response.
open_questions: How are stray-dog reports received, prioritized, and resolved?
When a dog cannot enter care, what happens next and why?

threads.title: Shelter and foster capacity
threads.summary: Examine where dogs wait for safe care and how shelter space, foster homes, recovery space, and everyday care affect movement through the system.
open_questions: Where are dogs waiting, and what suitable foster or recovery space is missing?
Which constraints could the proposed Canine Campus address, and which would remain?

threads.title: Veterinary care
threads.summary: Investigate how sterilization, treatment, appointment availability, transport, cost, and recovery capacity affect safe placement.
open_questions: Where do cost or appointment availability block care or placement?
What happens between a spay/neuter appointment and a safe recovery placement?

threads.title: Public access and coordination
threads.summary: Test whether residents and volunteers can reach the right people, get clear instructions, and participate. Communication or onboarding friction remains a hypothesis until verified.
open_questions: Can residents obtain timely guidance when they report or find a dog?
Where, if anywhere, do volunteer onboarding, scheduling, or coordination stall?

threads.title: Rescue, reunification, and adoption
threads.summary: Trace what helps or delays dogs leaving shelter care for reunification, rescue transfer, foster care, or adoption.
open_questions: What delays a dog that is ready for a safe placement?
Which handoffs between the shelter, rescues, fosters, and adopters need support?
How often do behavioral problems contribute to dog surrenders, and what training, assessment, or other support could prevent surrender or enable safe placement?

threads.title: Housing and prevention
threads.summary: Investigate whether pet-inclusive housing and other practical support can keep people and dogs together and prevent a crisis.
open_questions: Which housing or shelter rules prevent people and dogs from staying together?
Which supports could prevent dogs from entering crisis?
How often do housing and insurance breed restrictions prevent people from keeping or adopting dogs in Stockton?

title: Direct conversations and field visits
summary: We're contacting local responders and trying ways to help firsthand.

next_step.title: Visit a reported stray-dog location
next_step.summary: Go to a safe, publicly accessible location in Stockton where stray dogs have been reported. Observe conditions firsthand and look for evidence of unmet needs and existing responses. Do not approach unfamiliar dogs.

open_questions: What does getting started require?
What work is most useful to responders?
What prevents willing people from participating?

questions: What is the current status of Canine Campus?
What are the next milestones and obstacles?
What other major developments are underway?
What help is most needed right now?
Are there specific approved tasks with a location, schedule, supplies, and participation requirements?
If five new volunteers were available tomorrow, what could they actually do?
What coordination problems prevent willing people from helping?
